opts: -ān is feminine; the drill asks for masculine.

q: Exercise 2. Root ʿ-b-d: “You (f.sg) are making.”
opts: Without the enclitic this is “she is making.”

q: Exercise 2. Root ʿ-b-d: “They (m.pl) are making.”
opts: Right: the plural ending already shows the subject.
The 3rd-person enclitic is not used here.

q: Exercise 3. Translate: ʾĀzel-nā l-malkūttā.
opts: I am going to the kingdom.
He is going to the kingdom.
The participle is present; “went” is Perfect.
I am going from the kingdom.

q: Exercise 3. Translate: Šāmʿīn-tūn meltā d-Alāhā.
opts: You all are hearing the word of God.
We are hearing the word of God.
They are hearing the word of God.
3rd person takes no enclitic; -tūn is 2 m.pl.
You all are writing the word of God.

q: Exercise 3. Translate: Barnāšā bīšā rādep l-Yūḥannan.
opts: The evil man is pursuing Yukhannan.
Yukhannan is pursuing the evil man.
The good man is pursuing Yukhannan.

q: Exercise 3. Translate: Ḥāzēn-ḥnan nūhrā rabbā tammān.
opts: We are seeing a great light there.
We are seeing a great light here.
You are seeing a great light there.
We are seeing a great king there.

opts: Šmaʿ is the Perfect, not the participle.

q: Exercise 4. Render: “She is writing a good word.”
opts: Right: feminine participle and feminine adjective.
